MIZORAM PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
GENERAL COMPETITIVE EXAMINATIONS FOR RECRUITMENT TO THE POST OF
TRANSLATOR UNDER ART & CULTURE DEPARTMENT,
GOVERNMENT OF MIZORAM. MAY, 2019
GENERAL ENGLISH
Time Allowed : 3 hours
Full Marks : 100
Attempt all questions.
SECTION - A
(42 Marks)
This Section should be answered only on the Answer Sheet provided.
1. ‘Strong cultural values keep one rooted in modern times.’ Express your view on this statement in
about 400 – 500 words.
(20)
2. Read the following excerpt from a letter sent by Jawaharlal Nehru to his daughter Indira on her 13th
birthday and write the summary.
(10)
Central Prison, Nainital
October 26, 1930
On your birthday you have been in the habit of receiving presents and good wishes. Good wishes you
will still have in full measure, but what present can I send you from Naini Prison? My presents cannot
be very material or solid. They can be of the mind and spirit, such as a good fairy might have bestowed
on you - things that even the high walls of prison cannot stop.
You know sweetheart, how I dislike sermonising and doling out good advice. When I am tempted to
do this, I always think of a ‘very wise man’ I once read. Perhaps one day you will yourself read the
book which contains this story. I have always thought that the best way to find out what is right and
what is not right, what should be done and what should not be done, is not by giving a sermon, but by
talking and discussing, and out of discussion sometimes a little bit of truth comes out. I have liked
my talks with you and we have discussed many things, but the world is wide and beyond our world
lie other wonderful and mysterious worlds; so none of us need ever be bored or imagine that we have
learned everything worth learning and become very wise.
A letter can hardly take the place of a talk; at best it is a one-sided affair. So, if I say anything that
sounds like good advice do not take it as if it were a bad pill to swallow. Imagine that I have made a
suggestion to you for you to think over, as if we really were having a talk.
In history we read of great periods in the life of nations, of great men and women and great deeds
performed, and sometimes in our dreams and reveries we imagine ourselves back in those times and
doing brave deeds like the heroes of old. Do you remember how fascinated you were when you first
read the story of Jeanne d’Arc, and how your ambition was to be something like her? Ordinary men
and women are not usually heroic. They think of their bread and butter, of their children, of their
household worries and the like. But a time comes when a whole people become full of faith for a
great cause and then even simple, ordinary men and women become heroes, and history becomes

- 2 -
stirring and epoch-making. Great leaders have something in them which inspire a whole people and
make them do great deeds… In India a great leader, full of love for all who suffer and eager to help
them, has inspired our people to great actions and noble sacrifice. He has helped to make the starving,
the poor and the oppressed free and happy.
If we are to be India’s soldiers we have to respect India’s honour, and that honour is a sacred trust.
Often we may be in doubt as to what to do. It is no easy matter to decide what is right and what is
not. One little test I shall ask you to apply whenever you are in doubt. Never do anything in secret
or anything that you would wish to hide. For the desire to hide anything means that you are afraid,
and fear is a bad thing and unworthy of you. Be brave, and all the rest follows. If you are brave, you
will not fear and will not do anything of which you are ashamed. You know that in our great Freedom
Movement, under Bapuji’s leadership, there is no room for secrecy or hiding. We have nothing to
hide. We are not afraid of what we do or what we say. We work in the sun and in the light. Even so
in our private lives let us make friends with the sun and work in the light and do nothing secretly or
furtively. Privacy, of course, we may have and should have, but that is a very different thing from
secrecy. And if you do so, my dear you will grow up a child of the light, unafraid and serene and
unruffled, whatever may happen.
I have written a very long letter to you. And yet there is so much I would like to tell you. How can a
letter contain it?
Good-bye, little one, and may you grow up into a brave soldier in India’s service.
With all my love and good wishes.
3. Write a paraphrase of the following verse :
(6)
The glories of our blood and state
Are shadows, not substantial things:
There is no armour against fate;
Death lays his icy hands on kings;
Sceptre and Crown
Must tumble down.
And in the dust be equal made
With the poor crooked scythe and spade.
4. Translate the following paragraph from Mizo to English.
(6)
Mi chungchanga ngaih dân kan siam hian hmuh hmaih kan nei châwk. Chu chu ‘tumna a awm chuan
kawng a awm,’ tih hi a ni. Ka hmêl hriat, pa pakhat chuan tumah hneh a nei lo va; mahse, insuala
nguiban thei an awm miah lo thung. He pa hi a luhlul a, a huai a, a chhel êm êm a, engahmah hian
tlawm a tum ngai lo. A tâwpa tâwpah chuan a aia chakte pawhin an ngam peih tawh lo mai \hin. Rilru
chhungrila tumruhna inphûm te, rualawhna te, taihmâkna te, chhelna te, hlawhchham tum lohna awm
te hi kan inhmuhpui zo vek sêng ngai lo. Khaw khat nula hmêl\ha leh fel neitu chu mi hmêl\ha ber leh
hausa ber an ni chuang lo. ‘Saw pa nupui atan saw chuan ka va ui e,’ i tih chuan, saw pa saw i hre
chiang lo a ni. A nupuiin amaha thil hlu inphûm a hmuh i hmu ve lo tlat alawm!

SECTION - B
(58 Marks)
All questions carry equal marks of 1 each. Attempt all questions.
This Section should be answered only on the OMR Response Sheet provided.
Direction (Questions 1 - 8) : Choose the correct alternative closest in meaning to the underlined
idioms & phrases.
1. I have hit upon a good plan to get rid of him.
(a) started
(b) found
(c) forgone
(d) given up
2. He backed up his friend’s claim.
(a) gave up
(b) opposed
(c) swindled
(d) supported
3. When does the Convocation come off?
(a) take place
(b) complete
(c) begin
(d) end
4. The belief in witchcraft is losing ground.
(a) becoming less acceptable
(b) becoming stronger
(c) unlawful
(d) gaining popularity
5. It is a far cry from Delhi to New York.
(a) a great difference
(b) a long way off
(c) a painful journey
(d) a popular city
6. The scheme came to grief owing to want of foresight.
(a) failed
(b) made people sad
(c) succeeded
(d) was popular
7. One who lives a fast life often dies an early death.
(a) is unhealthy
(b) lives carelessly
(c) lives in pleasures
(d) drives very fast
8. That territory is a bone of contention.
(a) a subject of content
(b) a subject of dispute
(c) not regarded important
(d) a very crucial area
Direction (Questions 9 - 16) : Choose the most appropriate idioms & phrases from the given options to
make complete sentences.
9. The beautiful landscape of Mizoram _____________.
(a) beggars description
(b) is few and far between
(c) wins laurels
(d) is a turning point
10. If you are not successful, do not _____________. Try out something new.
(a) ride rough-shod
(b) harp on the same string.
(c) take the bull by the horns
(d) carry the day

(a) followed suit
(b) were up and doing
(c) beat about the bush
(d) played fast and loose

(a) blew his own trumpet
(b) cut a fine figure
(c) moved heaven and earth
(d) kicked up a row
13. In a hurry to reach my office, I left everything lying _____________.
(a) free and easy
(b) hard and fast
(c) at sixes and sevens
(d) null and void
14. The father’s criticism _____________ his child’s hope of success.
(a) fell flat on
(b) at daggers drawn
(c) few and far between
(d) threw cold water on
15. He is _____________ sixty.
(a) on the wrong side of
(b) over and above
(c) through and through
(d) on the brink of
16. Can you tell me the _____________ of his long speech?
(a) right and left
(b) sum and substance
(c) rank and file
(d) better-half

Direction (Questions 38 - 42) : Choose the correct passive form of the following sentences from the
given options.
38. We admire the brave.
(a) The brave are admired.
(b) The brave are to be admired.
(c) People admire the brave.
(d) The brave is to be admired.
39. Shall I ever forget those happy days?
(a) Those happy days will not be forgotten.
(b) Will those happy days be ever forgotten?
(c) Shall the happy days be forgotten by me?
(d) Should those happy days be ever forgotten?
40. My captors were taking me to prison.
(a) I was being taken to prison by my captors.
(b) I was taken to prison by my captors.
(c) My captors took me to prison.
(d) They were taking me to prison.
41. One should keep one’s promises.
(a) One’s promises are to be kept.
(b) Promises are to be kept by one.
(c) Promises should be kept.
(d) Keep your promises.
42. He showed me the greatest respect.
(a) I was shown respect greatly.
(b) Great respect was shown to me.
(c) He was showing me the greatest respect.
(d) I was shown the greatest respect.
Direction (Questions 43 - 58) : Choose the most suitable word from the given options.
43. My friend and mentor _____________ arrived.
(a) has
(b) is
(c) must
(d) have
44. The flower _____________.
(a) smells sweetly
(b) is sweet
(c) smells sweet
(d) sweetly smells
45. Solomon was the _____________ men.
(a) wisest of all
(b) wiser
(c) wise
(d) wiser of all
46. I _____________ the book on the table.
(a) lay
(b) lied
(c) lain
(d) laid
47. The news is _____________ good to be true.
(a) very
(b) too
(c) so
(d) extremely

48. I shall not come _____________ you need me.
(a) unless
(b) before
(c) since
(d) lest
49. I thanked the guests _____________ the staff.
(a) in honour of
(b) for the sake of
(c) on behalf of
(d) in lieu of
50. We must _____________ ourselves to the new environment.
(a) adhere
(b) adapt
(c) accede
(d) cling
51. The doctor _____________ the medicine for his sickness.
(a) has prescribed
(b) has proscribed
(c) has prescripted
(d) have prescribed
52. The _____________ to this office is prohibited.
(a) admission
(b) admittance
(c) attendance
(d) entrance
53. The court rejected his _____________ for mercy.
(a) request
(b) application
(c) petition
(d) pardon
54. One who can use both hands equally well is called_____________.
(a) Bidexterous
(b) Ambidexterous
(c) Biped
(d) Ambiguous
55. A _____________ of goods was delivered by the transport agency.
(a) regiment
(b) company
(c) consignment
(d) train
56. Please prepare a _____________ of books.
(a) list
(b) library
(c) table
(d) catalogue
57. He is my _____________. We work in the same office.
(a) colleague
(b) collegiate
(c) matinee
(d) coach
58. _____________ is the study of various races of mankind.
(a) Anthropology
(b) Ethnology
(c) Hematology
(d) Etymology
